analysis.title: Hartnett: The Sell Signal Is Over, Now Watch Chip Prices
key_insights: BofA Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.4 from 8.1, dropping below 8.0 and ending the sell signal triggered May 26. The drop was driven by weaker global stock breadth, bearish hedge fund positioning in oil and S&P 500 futures, less bullish gold futures positioning and weaker HY and EM debt flows. Stronger tech inflows were the only offset.

Sell signal scorecard since May 26: S&P 500 +3.0% (max drawdown -4.5%), Nasdaq 100 -0.2% (max drawdown -11.3%), MSCI ACWI +1.1% (max drawdown -4.4%), JNK -4.1% (max drawdown -4.7%). Historically there were 17 sell signals since 2002, with an average 2-3% global stock loss over 2-3 months, a hit ratio near 60% and max drawdowns of 15-20%. Index-level this one missed, but tech and junk bonds took the losses.
The 'old' Bull & Bear Indicator is at 5.1, down from 5.6 last week and a peak of 8.0 on September 1. FMS positioning remains at the 100th percentile ('V Bullish').

Sentiment has cooled but positioning has not. 2026 is on pace for record equity fund inflows: global stocks annualizing $1.3tn, US equities $636bn, IG bonds $480bn, tech funds $196bn (more than 2.5x the previous record) and Korea equities $76bn. Consumer funds show a record $18bn annualized outflow.

KOSPI is down 30% from its June peak, yet for every $100 of Korea inflow YTD only $7 has flowed out since the August peak. Foreigners were selling this week and buybacks are almost over, which suggests the real selling has not started.

EPFR flows for the week ending Wednesday: $64.5bn to stocks, $11.8bn to bonds, $0.1bn to gold, $0.6bn out of crypto, $53.1bn out of cash. Treasuries took a $3.6bn inflow, the 16th straight weekly inflow and the longest streak since August 2024. US stocks took $39.1bn and tech $10.7bn in the week the AI trade cracked.
BofA private clients hold a record 66.4% of $4.7tn in stocks and a record-low 9.3% in cash. Even the richest investors are not underweight risk.

Hartnett leans risk-off for the next 3-4 weeks, citing 3% real yields, the need for the Fed to hike on Oct 28, US/Iran/Russia/Ukraine/oil, rising risk of a 'wave-like' Democratic sweep in the midterms, and price action in AI spenders and lenders (PSP, BIZD, ORCL CDS).

The 10-year real yield is 2.9%, close to the 3% level that has coincided with breaks (GFC above 3%, tech bubble above 4%, plus Truss and SVB on a smaller scale). PSP and BIZD are back at 1H26 lows, and Oracle's 5-year CDS has gone parabolic while broad IG tech spreads are little changed.

Goldman's David Curtin ('Are higher yields beginning to cause cracks?') names two stress points: the French OAT rout and AI buildout financing, especially neoclouds. An all-in 6-8% cost of 10-year debt is manageable for hyperscalers expecting returns in the teens but bites faster for sub-investment grade borrowers. CoreWeave 2031s hit 1,100 bps over Treasuries. Curtin says markets will struggle to hold terminal rates at clearly restrictive levels because it is causing cracks in bond markets, and that AI pressure comes from financing cost and scale, not compressed returns.

Consensus hyperscaler capex is $807bn in 2026 and $1.16tn in 2027, with free cash flow of -$63bn this year and -$163bn next, so the gap must be financed by lenders. Goldman's Privorotsky says the AI unwind has entered phase two.

Hartnett still expects a Fed hike on Oct 28 to restore credibility (66 consecutive months of CPI above 2%) and to lower long-end yields by another 20bps. Market pricing disagrees: October hike odds topped 50% after hot CPI, then fell to 14% after Warsh gave no guidance. Goldman's Hatzius expects a pause in October and a final hike in December. Hartnett expects stocks to fall at least 10% in a Democratic sweep.

Breadth: 355 S&P 500 stocks are 10% or more below 52-week highs, 188 are 20% or more below and 93 are 30% or more below. BofA's Breadth Rule shows a net 52% of global indices oversold, the most since April 2025. The contrarian buy signal triggers at net 88%, which Hartnett says is hard to reach near term unless the overbought US, Taiwan and Brazil indices fall 6-10%.
Strong dollar (+3.8% YTD) has pushed the Indian rupee, Indonesian rupiah and Turkish lira to or near record lows, with the yen 3% from 40-year lows. RBI and Bank Indonesia have intervened.

Positioning calls: add 'peak yield' beneficiaries (small caps, REITs, consumer discretionary), and do not add tech. The October FMS shows the most underweight consumer discretionary since July 2008 and the most overweight tech since August 2020. Longer term, stay long gold, commodities and EM, and reduce the secular underweight in bonds and China.

Hartnett's key call is to watch semiconductor prices. Fresh price gains are bullish and would see investors return to tech in mid-November and enter 2027 reversing 'short tech bond' positions. A rollover in semi prices would signal tighter AI credit, a top in AI capex growth and lower-than-expected 2027 nominal GDP growth, leaving returns driven by income rather than capital appreciation. The US semiconductor PPI has gone vertical after decades of decline, feeding nominal GDP, which is up 63% from the COVID low to $33tn.
YTD scoreboard: oil 70.0%, US stocks 13.1%, global stocks 10.2%, US dollar 3.8%, cash 2.9%, HY -0.9%, IG -3.2%, government bonds -4.4%, gold -4.5%, bitcoin -6.1%.
